evidence: Confirmed by the simulator source. The provisioning path reads only image COUNT, never resolution: static workers are a fixed integer knob (trace_to_two_pool.py:413 --encoder-workers; provisioned_ms = encoder_workers * t_end_ms at :523-529), and the dynamic schedule C(t)=clamp(ceil(q(t)/rho)) is built from the image-RATE signal q(t) resampled from NumImages counts (forecast_schedule.py:11,18-19,95-96,130-131). No provisioning input (--encoder-workers, rho, q(t), --worker-schedule) reads image_px. Resolution enters ONLY through per-forward service time: --image-px feeds EncoderCostModel (trace_to_two_pool.py:412,453,167-170); service is memoized by TOTAL image count at that fixed resolution (:322, docstring :34-45), so a size increase re-costs each forward (pure service-time inflation) without changing counts, batching, or worker count. Dispatch is greedy FIFO with a 64-image cap, freed/earliest-available worker takes the FIFO head unit (:308-309,317,327-334). Hence provisioned worker-time is invariant to image size 'because the schedule is driven by count and blind to size' -- a structural code property, exactly as claimed. Contrast with the engine-cost gap (absorbed by p90 headroom) also holds since that gap is service-time within a fixed schedule.
fix: None needed; the mechanism is a verifiable property of the scheduling code (count-driven provisioning, size only in the cost model).
